intro: A $285,000 home in Texas could cost considerably more each month than its mortgage principal and interest payment suggests. Local property taxes, homeowners insurance, municipal utility district taxes and association fees can significantly influence affordability.

Our free Texas mortgage calculator helps you estimate your complete monthly housing payment before purchasing a property. Whether you're buying in Houston, Dallas, Austin, San Antonio or a smaller Texas community, compare financing arrangements and determine how much house you can comfortably afford.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Texas?

blocks.markdown:
A $285,000 Texas home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,366.98.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. The interest rate, property taxes and insurance premiums are illustrative planning assumptions rather than current statewide averages.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Texas housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/TX/HSG495223), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $283,800 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $2,106, while the homeownership rate was 62.6%.

These historical figures include homeowners who purchased under different market conditions. They do not represent current property asking prices.

Housing costs in Austin and Dallas may differ considerably from those in El Paso, Lubbock or smaller communities. Newly constructed homes may also have additional district taxes and association obligations.

Research recent comparable property sales and recurring ownership expenses before establishing your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Texas Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the expected purchase price of your property and your available down payment.

Choose your preferred mortgage term and enter your lender's quoted annual interest rate. If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees.

Add private mortgage insurance if required by your conventional financing arrangement.

Review the monthly payment breakdown and adjust individual inputs to compare borrowing scenarios.

The amortization schedule shows how much of each mortgage payment goes toward interest and reducing your outstanding loan balance.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing arrangements outside Texas.

sections.heading: How Texas Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Texas does not levy a state property tax. Instead, local taxing authorities establish property taxes to support public schools, counties, municipalities and other public services.

County appraisal districts determine property valuations and administer applicable exemptions.

A property's taxable value can differ between taxing jurisdictions because different exemptions may apply.

### Texas residence homestead exemption

Under the current [Texas Tax Code, Section 11.13](https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.11.htm), qualifying residence homesteads generally receive a $140,000 school district property tax exemption.

Eligible homeowners aged 65 or older or with qualifying disabilities receive an additional $60,000 school district exemption.

Other taxing authorities may offer separate local exemptions.

The general school district exemption does not automatically reduce taxable value by $140,000 for every county, city or special district tax calculation.

Contact your local appraisal district to confirm eligibility and application requirements.

### Texas homestead appraisal cap

The [Texas Comptroller's appraisal limitation guidance](https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/property-tax/appraisal-tax-limitations.php) explains that qualifying residence homesteads generally have a 10% annual limitation on appraised value growth, excluding qualifying new improvements.

This limitation applies to eligible appraised values rather than the final property tax bill.

Following an ownership transfer, a property may lose the benefit of the previous owner's capped appraisal.

Request an updated tax estimate instead of relying exclusively on the seller's historical property tax bill.

### Municipal utility district taxes

Some Texas properties are located within municipal utility districts, commonly known as MUDs.

These districts may collect additional property taxes to fund infrastructure such as water and wastewater services.

Two similarly priced homes may have different property tax obligations because one is located within a special taxing district.

Check the property's tax records and ask your real estate professional about applicable district taxes and outstanding assessments.

Include these charges in your annual property tax estimate without counting them twice.

Texas homeowners may experience hailstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes, wildfires and flooding.

Insurance premiums depend on property location, roof condition, construction materials, replacement cost and selected coverage.

Obtain written insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Coastal windstorm insurance

The [Texas Department of Insurance's windstorm guidance](https://www.tdi.texas.gov/tips/what-is-windstorm-insurance.html) explains that some coastal homeowners policies exclude wind and hail damage.

Eligible property owners may obtain separate coverage through the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association or another insurer.

Ask your lender and insurance agent whether separate windstorm protection or property certification is required.

### Flood insurance

Ordinary homeowners insurance generally excludes flood damage.

This is an important consideration for coastal properties and inland communities exposed to heavy rainfall.

Review the state's [flood insurance resources](https://www.tdi.texas.gov/consumer/storms/flood-insurance.html) and investigate your property's location through the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Include additional premiums for applicable flood and windstorm policies in your mortgage estimate.
The following estimates assume 20% down, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete monthly housing payments rather than relying exclusively on principal and interest.

The Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs, commonly known as TDHCA, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through approved lenders.

### My First Texas Home

The [My First Texas Home program](https://welcomehome.tdhca.texas.gov/products/my-first-texas-home) serves qualifying first-time homebuyers and eligible veterans.

Borrowers may receive down payment and closing cost assistance of up to 5% of their qualifying mortgage amount.

The program generally requires a minimum credit score of 620, approved homebuyer education and compliance with applicable income and purchase price limits.

### My Choice Texas Home

The [My Choice Texas Home program](https://welcomehome.tdhca.texas.gov/products/my-choice-texas-home) is available to qualifying first-time and repeat buyers.

It also offers assistance of up to 5% of the eligible mortgage amount.

Available arrangements include interest-free deferred repayable financing and conditionally forgivable secondary financing.

For example, 5% assistance on an eligible $228,000 mortgage would provide $11,400 toward qualifying purchase expenses.

Assistance-based mortgages may carry higher interest rates than loans without assistance. Compare the complete borrowing costs and request written repayment conditions before applying.

sections.heading: How Your Down Payment Changes Your Texas Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
A larger down payment reduces the amount you need to borrow.

For a $285,000 home, increasing your down payment from 10% to 20% requires an additional $28,500 upfront.

At an illustrative 6% interest rate over 30 years, this reduces your monthly principal and interest payment by approximately $170.87.

You may also avoid conventional private mortgage insurance by making the larger down payment.

However, retaining sufficient emergency savings may be more practical than committing every available dollar to the purchase.

Compare both scenarios using the calculator before deciding.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Texas Home

blocks.markdown:
Homeowners should consider summer cooling expenses, foundation maintenance, roof repairs and landscaping costs.

Buyers purchasing newly constructed homes should investigate whether existing property taxes reflect only undeveloped land rather than the completed residence.

An initial escrow estimate based on land-only taxation can result in a substantial payment increase when the completed property is assessed.

Use our [Texas Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/texas-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate take-home earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing financial obligations.

Texas does not impose an individual state income tax, but federal income taxes and applicable payroll deductions still affect household income.

Compare mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $285,000 Texas home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, principal and interest would be approximately $1,366.98 monthly. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total payment.

### What is the Texas homestead exemption in 2026?

Qualifying residence homesteads generally receive a $140,000 school district property tax exemption. Eligible homeowners aged 65 or older or with qualifying disabilities receive an additional $60,000 exemption. Local exemptions may also apply.

### Does Texas offer down payment assistance?

Yes. TDHCA offers eligible borrowers assistance of up to 5% of their qualifying mortgage amount through programs such as My First Texas Home and My Choice Texas Home. Eligibility and repayment conditions vary.

Use our Texas mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, down payments, interest rates and repayment periods.

Replace illustrative property taxes and insurance premiums with verified property-specific estimates. Understanding local exemptions, district taxes and complete insurance requirements can help you establish a sustainable homebuying budget.
